claim_lines.38: Under AC and DC, finitely many ordinary blowups at singular closed points resolve the given rational Gorenstein normal local surface domain; every model remains normal, has rational closed local rings and invertible canonical module; the terminal model is regular and projective, and the composite is unchanged off the original closed point.
claim_lines.48-50: A point blowup retains the canonical pullback properties and rationality propagates to local rings.
claim_lines.52-56: The tangent-conic Hilbert function and nonsquare/square cases govern singular successors; in the square case a nonzero cubic on the reduced exceptional line contains all singular successors.
claim_lines.58-60: Double-plus-simple and triple-cubic branch lemmas give termination for the remaining square branches.
claim_lines.68: Each blowup preserves normality, rationality, canonical invertibility and projectivity in the stated setting.
claim_lines.70-74: Nonsquare chains terminate; square points have finitely many cubic-controlled successors and at most one continuing square successor; the rooted singular-successor tree is finitely branching with no infinite branch.
claim_lines.76-78: Blowing up the finite tree's nodes in ancestor order gives the finite sequence; each map is an isomorphism away from its center, and all centers lie over the original closed point.

reviews.diagram_kind: finite branching tree of singular-point blowups followed by an ancestor-ordered resolution sequence
reviews.reason: The proof's termination argument is explicitly a finitely branching tree, with different tangent-conic and cubic branches. A tree diagram can show why branch termination and finite branching yield a finite sequence and where the exceptional loci lie. It is an editorial aid: the proof already supplies the argument, and no uniqueness of centers or resolution sequence is asserted.

proposed_diagram.initial_model: X₀=Spec A with original closed point p₀ singular.

branch_tree.edge: A node is a singular closed point p on a model X_j; an edge to a successor q denotes the ordinary blowup Bl_p(X_j)→X_j followed by a singular closed point q on the new model over p.
branch_tree.nonsquare_case: If the tangent-conic quadratic is not a scalar square, its singular-point chain terminates in a regular model.
branch_tree.square_case: For square tangent conic, place singular successors among the closed zeros of the nonzero cubic H on the reduced exceptional line (at most three distinct closed zeros). Simple zeros have nonsquare successor conic; the triple-cubic case has at most one multiple closed zero of degree one.
branch_tree.remaining_branches: Double-plus-simple branches terminate; cube branches enter the nonsquare or double-plus-simple case after at most two further square successors. Mark no more than one continuing square successor at a node.
branch_tree.termination: Every node has finitely many successors; branch lemmas rule out infinite paths; DC yields finiteness of the rooted tree.

proposed_diagram.finite_resolution: Blow up the finitely many nodes in ancestor order, yielding X_N→⋯→X₁→X₀. Label each center a singular closed point and each map projective and an isomorphism away from its center.
proposed_diagram.labels: At every stage: normal model; closed local rings rational; canonical module invertible. Terminal X_N regular. All centers lie over p₀, so the composite is an isomorphism off p₀.
proposed_diagram.caveat: Draw one valid finite tree/sequence without asserting it is unique or canonical. Do not label exceptional fibres as P¹; the text only specifies a reduced exceptional line in the cubic-control statement.

mathematical_check.objects_and_maps: X₀=Spec A is a normal local surface; each edge is an ordinary blowup at a singular closed point on the current model. The resulting models map projectively to the local base, and each blowup is an isomorphism off its center.
mathematical_check.branching_and_termination: A square-conic node's singular successors lie in the zero scheme of a nonzero cubic on the reduced exceptional line, hence form a finite set with at most three distinct closed points. Simple-zero, double-plus-simple, cube, and nonsquare cases are treated by the cited branch lemmas. The proof uses finite branching plus no infinite path and DC to conclude the tree is finite.
mathematical_check.propagation: The stated blowup supplier and proof step 1.1 preserve normality, rationality of closed local rings, invertibility of the canonical module, and normal completion at every stage. The terminal model is regular after blowing up all nodes.
mathematical_check.support_and_composite: Centers remain over the original closed point; composing blowups is therefore an isomorphism on the complement of that point. Projectivity follows at each point blowup and hence for the composite.
mathematical_check.uniqueness: No uniqueness claim follows from the theorem or proof; a diagram should depict a possible finite branch tree and ancestor-ordered sequence only.
mathematical_check.result: No inconsistency found in the stated branch termination, finite-tree construction, normality/rationality propagation, terminal regularity, or off-center isomorphism claims.
